hypothesis: A semantic family-head projection maintained before the cognitive hot read can retain grouped possibility accuracy while making the hot read equivalent to an ordinary indexed Top-K lookup.
counterhypothesis: The gain is only hidden query work; build/update costs or a conventional database query can dominate once the same family semantics are implemented honestly.
scope_guard: Same SQLite engine is used for all physical baselines. This is a synthetic possibility-family workload, not proof of universal superiority over every database or real Frank task accuracy.

semantics.flat_baseline: candidate ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT K
semantics.correct_query_time_sql: ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY family ORDER BY score DESC,binding) then rn=1 then global Top-K
semantics.preprocessor_projection: one current best binding per explicit family in family_head, indexed by global score; hot read is family_head ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT K
semantics.targeted_update: recompute only changed family head using family-local index, UPSERT family_head, then read indexed Top-K

interpretation: Flat Top-K is a latency floor but spends most of a bounded model-context budget on duplicate bindings and therefore has poor family coverage in this fixture.
Correct SQL grouping restores family coverage but repeats grouping/window work at query time.
Materialized family heads move that semantic work to compile/update time and make the hot read as simple as the flat index read while preserving grouped accuracy.
The physical implementation can still be SQLite: the architectural distinction is semantic preprocessing, not rejection of database storage engines.

At 160k rows the local median initial build amortizes after about 1.23 grouped reads under this stable fixture; real EAP must use measured lifetime/read-update economics rather than assuming this rate universally.
promotion_gate: Integrate explicit family-head semantics with current EAP/ClayGraph provenance and negative-space gates rather than a parallel standalone store.
Run exact current-main EAP F1/F2/F3 mechanisms on the verified self-hosted Ubuntu target runner.
Measure storage/write amplification and concurrent epoch publication/recovery.
Compare against current simpler authoritative SQLite rank-index baseline and exact-key bypass.
Measure downstream fixed-context model/task/tool-route accuracy, not only family retrieval coverage.
